what_its_for: Naldemedine is used to treat constipation caused by opioid pain medicines (such as morphine, oxycodone, or hydrocodone) in adults who have ongoing (chronic) pain that is not related to cancer. It works by blocking the effect that opioid medicines have on your bowels, helping you have more regular bowel movements without affecting your pain relief.
how_to_take: Take naldemedine by mouth as a tablet, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet.
dosing: The usual dose is one 0.2 mg tablet taken once daily. Always take the dose exactly as your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than prescribed without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store naldemedine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in the original packaging away from light and moisture. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking naldemedine with grapefruit or grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid starting or stopping other medicines without telling your doctor, especially rifampin (an antibiotic) or certain antifungal medicines, as they can change how well naldemedine works. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you have: severe stomach pain, cramping, or diarrhea that does not stop; signs of opioid withdrawal such as sweating, chills, runny nose, feeling anxious, yawning, fast heartbeat, or goosebumps; or a tear or hole in your stomach or intestines (signs include sudden severe belly pain, fever, or vomiting). Also call your doctor if your constipation does not improve or if you notice any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Naldemedine usually starts working within a few days of starting treatment. Most people begin to notice more regular bowel movements within the first week. Continue taking it every day as directed for the best results, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as opioid withdrawal can occur in an unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine, as it may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. If you have liver problems, especially severe liver disease, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine, as a lower dose or extra monitoring may be needed. This medicine has not been studied extensively in children and is approved for use in adults only.
